advice: Abstain. No distinct scratch-lifetime change is supported by the supplied evidence: the active panel32 path already allocates one 64 KiB scratch area per gemm call, overwrites it during packing, and uses it across the panel computation. The proposed 4 KiB K-block buffer would require repacking and consuming each K block while keeping all four ZA accumulators live; that adds loop and packing work, with no supplied evidence that scratch reservation or initialization limits throughput. The prior pointer-scheduling experiment and its noisy results do not test this idea.
risks: Changing scratch lifetime or packing cadence could add overhead or disturb operand bounds, stack handling, or FP32 update order. If reconsidered, validate the full 512-step reduction, stack alignment and ABI, timed packing/allocation, all 48 public cases at tolerance 0.002, then ten validation reports and ten alternating paired controls under unchanged settings. Do not infer a gain from the prior joint outcome.
